title: Rope access and anchor certification
audience: Owners, supervisors and quoting staff on the window cleaning (all heights) track who may be asked to offer or price rope-access work. Not a rope-access course and not a certification pathway.
learningOutcomes: Explain why rope access is a specialist method that this course does not teach or certify.
Identify the anchor and equipment checks that a competent person must complete before rope access is considered.
Decide whether a higher-rate rope-access quote is supportable on the evidence available.

instruction.heading: What rope access is, and why it is restricted
instruction.body: Rope access uses ropes and harnesses to move a worker down or across a surface, usually with a second rope or line as a backup. It is a specialist method. It depends on correctly rated anchors, rope systems that have been inspected, and a worker who has been trained and assessed to use them. A worker who has completed a window cleaning course has not thereby become competent in rope access. This lesson is about recognising that boundary, not about learning the method.

instruction.heading: The standard that applies to fall arrest equipment
instruction.body: The ACT working-heights page says its competency-based fall arrest and travel restraint training follows AS/NZS 1891.4:2009 (no date shown). Do not describe the standard as a certification scheme. Equipment used for fall arrest should be selected, used and maintained as the manufacturer directs and in line with the relevant standard (text not read), and a competent person must decide whether it suits the task.

instruction.heading: Anchor evaluation
instruction.body: An anchor is only as good as its structure and its rating. Before a rope system is trusted, a competent person must confirm the anchor point's location, condition, load capacity and suitability for the surface. Anchors on old, corroded or unknown structures are not verified. Record anchor locations as unknown until verified, and refuse to use an anchor that cannot be verified.

instruction.heading: Stop-work and referral
instruction.body: Stop the job and refer it if the anchor is unverified, the rope or harness is damaged or out of date, the surface is unknown, the wind or weather changes, or the worker is not assessed for the method. Referral goes to the person who holds site authority and to the competent person who would supervise the method. Do not attempt a rope-access job as an improvisation to save time.

instruction.heading: Revenue and honest pricing
instruction.body: A rope-access job may command a higher hourly rate because of the specialist skill and equipment it needs. That higher rate is only supportable when the evidence shows verified competence, verified equipment, a verified anchor and written authority from the site controller. Under the Western Australian and Northern Territory quote rules, an accepted quote is binding, so its exclusions must be written into it. When the evidence is missing, quote only the ground-based or platform-based work that you are authorised to perform, and state in writing what is excluded.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, rope-access competence or authority to work on ropes or anchors. Completing this lesson is not evidence that a worker or business is certified for rope access. A business must not advertise rope-access certification unless it holds evidence of that certification from a verified source.

procedure: Confirm whether the job scope requires rope access, a platform or a ground-based method, and record the answer.
Ask for the anchor location, its condition, its load rating and the competent person who has verified it.
Check that each rope, harness and fall-arrest component has a current inspection record and the manufacturer's instructions.
If any anchor or component is unverified, record it as unknown and stop.
Confirm written authority from the site controller and the competent supervisor for the method.
Price only the work that the verified evidence supports, and state the exclusions in writing.
Record the referral, the decision and the person who owns the next step.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial client asks for a rope-access clean of a glazed atrium roof, and the quoting team wants to price it at a specialist rate. No anchor certificate or inspection record is available.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the specialist rate be quoted, and what is the next step?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The anchor is unverified and the worker's rope-access competence is not evidenced. Quote only what the business is authorised to do, state rope access as excluded, and refer the anchor question to a competent person. Record the request, the missing evidence and the decision owner before any rate is shown to the client.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor says a worker who has used a harness on a scaffold can also do rope access on a tall building.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the supervisor check before agreeing?
workedExamples.reasoning: Scaffold harness use is not the same as rope-access competence. The supervisor must check the worker's assessed competence for the specific method, the anchor, the rope system and the surface, and must confirm the authority and any state requirement. Until those are confirmed, the answer is no.

equipmentAndPpe: Job pack showing whether rope access, a platform or a ground-based method is in scope
Anchor verification record with location, condition and rating
Inspection records for ropes, harnesses and fall-arrest components
Written referral and authority record from the site controller and competent supervisor

commonErrors.error: Quoting a rope-access rate without verified competence or anchor evidence.
commonErrors.prevention: Price only what the verified evidence supports and state exclusions in writing.

commonErrors.error: Treating an unknown anchor as sound.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the anchor as unknown and refuse to use it until a competent person has verified it.

commonErrors.error: Assuming scaffold or harness experience equals rope-access competence.
commonErrors.prevention: Check assessed competence for the specific method, anchor and surface.

commonErrors.error: Advertising certification the business does not hold.
commonErrors.prevention: Only state certifications supported by verified evidence from the issuing body.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The ACT working-heights page names AS/NZS 1891.4:2009 as the basis for its fall arrest competency training (no date shown).
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or rope-access competence. The lesson does not describe a certification pathway.

The Safe Work Australia working-heights page places fall arrest last in its control order (no date shown). The model falls code states no hierarchy (no date shown), and its legal effect depends on each jurisdiction.

qualityStandard: Rope access is identified as out of scope unless verified competence, equipment and anchor evidence exist.
Every anchor is recorded as verified or unknown, and unknown anchors are not used.
Quotes state the exclusions in writing and reflect only evidenced work.
No certification is claimed without evidence from the issuing body.
documentationEvidence: Scope decision naming the method and the reason for it
Anchor verification record with the competent person who checked it
Equipment inspection records for rope, harness and fall-arrest components
Quote with exclusions and the referral decision on file
summary: Rope access is a specialist method that this course does not teach or certify.
Anchors and equipment are verified by a competent person before they are trusted.
A higher specialist rate is supportable only with verified competence, equipment and authority.
This lesson grants no licence, certificate or rope-access competence.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is rope access treated as a specialist method in this lesson?
options: It is cheaper than the other methods on the job, the crew and the van
It needs only a ladder, a bucket, a rag, a towel and a squeegee on the site
It depends on verified anchors, inspected rope systems and an assessed worker
It is always legal without any authority at all on any site or building

knowledgeChecks.question: An anchor has an unknown history and no load rating. How must it be recorded?
options: As safe because it looks solid to the eye
As verified by the customer on the day
As suitable for a single light worker only
As unknown until a competent person verifies it

knowledgeChecks.question: When is a specialist rope-access rate supportable?
options: When verified competence, equipment, anchor evidence and authority exist
Whenever a client asks for it on the phone or in writing today
Whenever the business has a ladder on the van and a rope too
Whenever the price is higher than the ground-based rate for the job

knowledgeChecks.question: What does this lesson say about rope-access certification in this draft?
options: It is confirmed in every state and territory of Australia by the regulator
It is not granted by this lesson, which gives no certification route
It is granted on completion of this lesson by the trainer
It is the same as a scaffold licence held by the business

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker has used a harness on scaffolding. Does this establish rope-access competence?
options: Yes, harness use is the same skill as rope access work on site
Yes, if the supervisor agrees to it in writing for the whole job
No, the worker must be assessed for the specific method, anchor and surface
Yes, if the job is on a single storey building in the city centre
